import pandas as pd
t = tables['trips']
t = t[t['cls'].isin(['three_quarter','overnight','day_1_5','hd_am','hd_pm','hd_unspecified','hd_twilight','full_day'])]

def bucket(doy):
    return (doy//20)*20

res = {}
for season in [1,2]:
    s = t[t['fish_date_season']==season].copy()
    s['bucket'] = bucket(s['fish_date_doy'])
    g = s.groupby('bucket').agg(yt=('yt','sum'), anglers=('anglers','sum'), n=('yt','size'))
    g['ypa'] = g['yt']/g['anglers']
    res[f'season{season}_by_doybucket'] = g[['ypa','n','yt','anglers']].round(3).to_dict('index')

# class breakdown for doy120-180 and doy180-320 each season
for season in [1,2]:
    s = t[(t['fish_date_season']==season)]
    for lo,hi,label in [(120,180,'120-180'),(180,240,'180-240'),(240,300,'240-300'),(300,335,'300-335')]:
        w = s[(s['fish_date_doy']>=lo)&(s['fish_date_doy']<hi)&(s['cls'].isin(['three_quarter','overnight','day_1_5']))]
        g = w.groupby('cls').agg(yt=('yt','sum'), anglers=('anglers','sum'), n=('yt','size'))
        g['ypa']=(g['yt']/g['anglers']).round(3)
        res[f'S{season}_{label}'] = g['ypa'].to_dict()

# recent trailing (last 14 days as of day 152, season 2) by class
recent = t[(t['fish_date_season']==2)&(t['fish_date_doy']>=138)&(t['fish_date_doy']<=152)&(t['cls'].isin(['three_quarter','overnight','day_1_5']))]
g = recent.groupby('cls').agg(yt=('yt','sum'), anglers=('anglers','sum'), n=('yt','size'))
g['ypa']=(g['yt']/g['anglers']).round(3)
res['S2_recent_d138_152'] = g[['ypa','n']].to_dict('index')

# ONI trend
c = tables['climate']
oni = c[c['index_id']=='oni'].sort_values('avail_doy')
res['oni_recent'] = oni[['avail_season','avail_doy','value']].tail(10).to_dict('records')

result = res

# dope_solo notes — living doc. Read top section first (current plan), history below.

## CURRENT PLAN — as of Season 2, day 152 planning turn (21:00)
Status: $1250/$2000, 9/10 PTO, PTO committed for d158. Season score 0.0244,
rank 14/34 — well below top agents (~0.6-0.7) who appear to just fish more
often on live signal, not from exotic modeling. **Diagnosis of the underperformance:
I've been too trigger-shy and too reactive to single-trip noise, so I've only
taken 5 cheap $150 probes all season (1 tiny hit, 4 zeros) while real signal
was sitting there unbooked.**

**Key finding this turn — I was faked out by single-trip noise on a boat that
is actually running hot:** San Diego 3Q trailing ypa over its last 10 trips
(d138-152) is **0.396** — one of the best sustained per-boat signals all
season. But my journal entries for d148-152 dismissed it as "stale/fading"
based on reading just the most recent 1-2 trips (which happened to be zero).
**Lesson: a single 0-yt trip on a boat with a strong multi-trip trailing
average is NOISE, not a trend reversal.** Going forward, track/trust a
rolling ~8-10 trip per-boat pooled ypa (yt sum / angler sum over the boat's
last ~10 sailings in that class), not the single most recent trip.

Full picture of the current (doy138-152) window, per-boat pooled ypa,
three_quarter and overnight (only boats with n>=2 trips):
- 3Q: **San Diego 0.396 (n=10)**, Mission Belle 0.221 (n=7), Dominator 0.18
  (n=2), Malihini 0.145 (n=11), New Seaforth 0.08, Fisherman III 0.069,
  Pacific Voyager 0.028, Point Loma 0.0, Sea Watch 0.0.
- Overnight: **Prowler 0.463 (n=3, small sample, watch)**, Mustang 0.167
  (n=3), Penetrator 0.0, Pride 0.0.
- Class-pooled ypa doy138-152: three_quarter 0.209 (n=44), overnight 0.242
  (n=15), day_1_5 weak 0.037 (n=7, still cold).

**This is real, tradeable signal right now.** San Diego 3Q and Prowler
overnight both clear any reasonable trigger. Season-2 doy120-180 window
overall is running at ~25-30% of season-1's level in the same window (S2
0.137/0.127/0.02 vs S1 0.467/0.5/0.239 for 3Q/overnight/day_1_5) — softer
than S1 but clearly not dead, and specific boats (San Diego, Prowler) are
running well above the class average.

**Decision for the nightly self, through ~doy180:**
1. Keep booking San Diego 3Q ($150, cheap, weekend-preferred for 0 PTO) as
   long as its trailing ~10-trip pooled ypa stays >0.25. Don't drop it after
   one zero trip — only step back if the trailing average itself falls
   below ~0.15-0.2.
2. Also test Prowler overnight ($400) — small sample (n=3) but 0.463 ypa is
   the best print of the window. Confirm with 1-2 more trips before scaling
   up spend on it.
3. Add Mission Belle 3Q as a secondary target (0.221 ypa, n=7) if San Diego
   isn't sailing or is fully booked by competitors.
4. Diversify across these 2-3 boats rather than fixating on one — reduces
   the chance of misreading single-boat variance as a trend change, and
   captures more of the real signal if the bite is broad.
5. day_1_5 stays cold in this window (0.037-0.02 ypa) — skip it here, save
   it for fall.
6. Still avoid HD_AM/HD_PM/TWILIGHT — confirmed dead for YT all season, both
   seasons, every window checked.
7. Budget/PTO check: $1250 and 9 PTO with ~130 days of season left is a
   healthy reserve. With a real live signal now, it's fine to spend faster
   than the $150-only pace of the last 2 months — e.g. a few $150 3Q trips
   plus a couple $400 overnight trips (Prowler) over the next 2-3 weeks is
   affordable and should not be blocked by over-caution, as long as ~$700-900
   and 6+ PTO are kept in reserve for the fall peak (see below).

**FALL PLAN — refined this turn, important correction:**
Season-1 fall breakdown by class (previous notes only had the pooled number):
- doy180-240 (early "trough"): 3Q 0.049, overnight 0.144, day_1_5 0.02 — all weak.
- doy240-300 (includes the known Sep/Oct peak): 3Q 0.122, overnight 0.272,
  **day_1_5 0.8**.
- doy300-335 (previously logged as "falling off" from a pooled-only view):
  3Q 0.055, overnight 0.184, **day_1_5 1.875 — actually the single best
  per-class ypa window found anywhere in either season, better than the
  280-300 pooled headline number (1.735).**
- **Correction to old plan: day_1_5 is the dominant fall vehicle, and its
  best window is LATER (doy~300-335) than the pooled "280-300 peak" label
  suggested. Don't assume the fall opportunity is over once doy300 pooled
  numbers look like they're declining — check day_1_5 specifically, it may
  still be climbing.** Overnight is the solid #2 fall class throughout
  240-335 (0.18-0.27). Three_quarter is comparatively weak in fall (0.05-0.12)
  — it's a spring/early-summer class, not a fall one.
- Start watching day_1_5 and overnight schedules/counts hard from ~doy250
  onward (a bit earlier than the old doy270-280 note, to not miss the ramp),
  and be ready to book day_1_5 ($550, needs 14-day PTO lead time!) through
  doy335 even if pooled headline numbers look like they're already fading.
  Remember day_1_5 PTO must be committed 14+ days ahead — start planning PTO
  commitments for likely fall weekday windows by ~doy265-270 at the latest.
- ONI: data pull this turn was inconsistent/hard to interpret (season
  indices didn't line up cleanly) — re-pull cleanly next planning turn with
  a season-2-only filter instead of trusting a quick multi-season dump.

**Process fix (most important takeaway):** my nightly self has been
under-trading a real signal by treating single-trip results as if they were
the whole trend. Next planning turn, check whether this was corrected —
did booking frequency pick up in the doy152-180 window on the San
Diego/Prowler/Mission Belle signal, and did trailing multi-trip ypa (not
last-trip) get used as the actual trigger?

**Next planning turn checks:**
1. Did doy152-180 booking increase versus the doy91-152 pace (5 trips in 60
   days is too sparse for a live signal)? If not, the process fix above
   didn't take — revisit.
2. Re-check San Diego/Mission Belle 3Q and Prowler/Mustang overnight
   trailing ypa — still hot, faded, or overtaken by a new boat?
3. Clean re-pull of season-2 ONI trend (filter avail_season==2 only) and
   pier temp vs season 1 at the same doy.
4. Start day_1_5 boat-level scouting once doy~250-260 data is in — which
   boats run day_1_5 in the fall window, any early signal.
5. Confirm PTO committed for d158 got used or expired; plan next PTO
   commitments (14-day lead) for any fall weekday day_1_5/overnight targets.

## Season-1 baseline reference (by class, doy bucket, ypa)
- HD_AM/HD_PM/TWILIGHT: dead all year, both seasons (~0.00-0.01). Never book.
- doy80-100: pooled 0.833 (spring spike).
- doy120-180: three_quarter 0.467, overnight 0.5, day_1_5 0.239 (second-best
  window of the year for 3Q/overnight).
- doy180-240: weak across the board (3Q 0.049, overnight 0.144, day_1_5 0.02).
- doy240-300: day_1_5 0.8, overnight 0.272, 3Q 0.122 (fall ramp-up).
- doy300-335: **day_1_5 1.875 (best of anywhere)**, overnight 0.184, 3Q 0.055.
- doy335+: dead (season ending).

## Season 2 timeline log (condensed)
- Doy1-91: cold La Niña start (ONI ~-1.6 to -1.3), pier temp colder than S1,
  trips table flat 0.000 through doy91 despite S1's spring spike there.
- Doy91-152 (nightly log): mostly stayed home on a discipline of requiring
  multi-day/multi-boat confirmation before testing. Booked 5 cheap ($150)
  three_quarter probes (San Diego mostly): d100 (share 0.024, small hit),
  d107/d113/d127/d148 (all zero). Correctly avoided some single-day-spike
  traps (d106, d112, d113 pooled fleet spikes that didn't hold on the actual
  booked boat) but **overcorrected into missing real signal**: San Diego 3Q
  was actually running 0.396 ypa over its last 10 trips as of d152, and I
  read it as "fading" off one bad trip instead of booking more.
- doy120-180 in S2 running softer than S1 (3Q 0.137, overnight 0.127, day_1_5
  0.02 vs S1's 0.467/0.5/0.239) but individual boats (San Diego 3Q, Prowler
  overnight) are running well above the class average — the edge is at the
  boat level, not just the class/window level.

## Open items
- Boat-level variance analysis: started this turn (see table above), keep
  updating each planning turn as new boats/data show up.
- No forum/submit_strategy tool available to this agent (solo variant) —
  decisions are notes.md + nightly briefing judgment only.
- Leaderboard shows several "books nothing" strategy strings with nonzero
  season_fish (e.g. calendarist 0.7045) — this is because solo-variant
  agents' actual bookings come from nightly judgment, not strategy.py; the
  strategy string is just the (unused) code file. Not a data anomaly, no
  action needed — but it's a reminder that top performers are simply
  fishing more/more accurately on live signal, which matches the process
  fix above.
